title: Longest Common Subsequence
keyIdea: Compare text1[i] with text2[j]. If they match, take the letter in both and move both on: 1 + lcs(i + 1, j + 1). If not, one of them is not used, so try skipping each: max(lcs(i, j + 1), lcs(i + 1, j)). That is n × m states; each row only needs the row below and the cell to its right, so two rows are enough.

approaches.name: Recursion
approaches.idea: Match → 1 + solve(i + 1, j + 1); no match → max(solve(i, j + 1), solve(i + 1, j)).
approaches.why: Two branches on every mismatch with nothing saved; the stack is up to n + m deep.
approaches.warn: Too slow for 1000-letter strings. It also passes both strings by value, so every call copies them.

approaches.name: Memoization
approaches.idea: Same recursion with strings by reference; save each (i, j) answer in dp.
approaches.why: n × m states with O(1) work each; dp table plus a stack up to n + m deep.

approaches.name: Tabulation
approaches.idea: dp of size (n + 1) × (m + 1), all 0. Fill i from n − 1 down and j from m − 1 down: match → 1 + dp[i + 1][j + 1], else max(dp[i + 1][j], dp[i][j + 1]). Answer dp[0][0].
approaches.why: Two nested loops; the whole table is kept.

approaches.name: Tabulation, two rows
approaches.idea: Your active code: row i reads only next (row i + 1) and curr[j + 1] (already filled, to the right), so keep two rows of m + 1; after each i, next = curr. Answer next[0].
approaches.why: Same two loops; only two rows of m + 1 are stored.

quiz.q: text1[i] == text2[j]. Why is it safe to take 1 + lcs(i + 1, j + 1) without also trying to skip?
options: Matching these two letters never gives a shorter answer than skipping one of them
Skipping is tried later by the loop
It isn't safe; it's a heuristic

quiz.q: On a mismatch, why max(lcs(i, j + 1), lcs(i + 1, j))?
options: At least one of the two letters is not in the common subsequence, so skip one or the other
Because the diagonal is always smaller
To avoid going out of bounds

quiz.q: In the two-row version, which cells does curr[j] read?
Why does dp have an extra row and column of 0s?
options: They stand for an empty rest of a string: LCS with nothing is 0

steps: Subsequence, not substring? Lowercase only? Lengths up to 1000?
Work abcde / ace by hand: which letters line up?
Brute force: every subsequence of one string, checked against the other. Cost?
